# Stored XSS via user-authored tool-call embeds in the Markdown renderer

## Summary
Any authenticated user can execute arbitrary JavaScript in other users' browsers by sending content shaped as a tool-call `<details>` block. The Markdown renderer parsed the block's `embeds` attribute without distinguishing server-generated tool-call output from user-authored input, decoded and JSON-parsed it, and mounted each element in a sandboxed iframe with scripts enabled, so it ran at render time for every viewer. The missing control is a trust gate separating user content from the tool-call embed path.

## Preconditions
An authenticated account on the instance. The primary demonstrated surface is channel messages, which requires the Channels feature enabled by an admin (`ENABLE_CHANNELS`, off by default); the same gadget also reaches main-chat user messages and citation previews of retrieved documents, which need no special feature flag. No elevated role is required. By default the embed iframe is sandboxed `allow-scripts` without `allow-same-origin`, so the injected script runs in an opaque origin.

## Impact
The injected script executes in a null-origin sandboxed iframe for anyone who views the message or opens the citation. In the default configuration it cannot read the viewer's session token or make same-origin authenticated requests; the confirmed default primitive is contained script execution and convincing in-app phishing content rendered inside the interface. Where an operator has turned on `iframeSandboxAllowSameOrigin`, the sandbox gains `allow-same-origin` and the script can read `localStorage` (session token) and act as the victim, raising the impact to session hijacking. The payload is stored, so it re-executes on every view.

## Fix
Fixed in 0.11.4 by PR #29985. Embed rendering is now opt-in: the flag defaults off and is forwarded through every Markdown render path, including the standalone tool-call branch, colon fences and alerts. Assistant responses opt in only for the viewer's own chat; channel messages and read-only/shared views pass it explicitly off, so user-authored content can no longer reach the embed iframe. Upgrading to 0.11.4 fully resolves the issue with no additional configuration.

## Root cause
The tool-call embed sink lives in the shared Markdown renderer: `ToolCallDisplay.svelte` and `ConsecutiveDetailsGroup.svelte` read the `embeds` attribute off a `<details type="tool_calls">` token and mount each element in `FullHeightIframe` with `allowScripts={true}`. The renderer never distinguished tokens produced by the tool-execution pipeline from tokens parsed out of arbitrary user-authored message content, and the later `allowEmbeds` guard was applied only to the grouped path, so a single standalone details block bypassed it entirely and reached the iframe on every surface that renders user content.

## Proof of concept
Reproduced on stock 0.11.3 with default settings and Channels enabled. A non-admin account posted a channel message whose content was `<details type="tool_calls" embeds="["<script>...</script>"]">...</details>`. Opening the channel rendered one iframe with `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-popups allow-downloads"` and the attacker HTML in `srcdoc`, and the injected script executed in the viewer's browser (null origin). The same message on 0.11.4 renders no iframe and no script runs.

## Credits
@KadirArslan: channel messages, original report and proof of concept.
@5yu4n: cross-user delivery through channel direct messages.
@ComputerOnFire: citation previews of knowledge-base documents, and the ungated standalone-block path.
